row.scim_price_text: Guard Standard: $4.20/user/mo (price shown with monthly billing); included at no extra cost in Atlassian Cloud Enterprise
row.team_price_text: Add-on on top of any Atlassian Cloud Standard or Premium subscription
row.evidence: Atlassian Guard Standard, $4.20 per user / month, includes "SCIM automated user provisioning"; Atlassian's provisioning docs list Atlassian Guard Standard as the requirement.
row.notes: SCIM (and SAML SSO) need the Atlassian Guard add-on, billed per user on top of Jira/Confluence/etc.; Cloud Enterprise includes Guard Standard. The pricing page's default price ($4.20 Standard, $8.18 Premium) is the monthly-billing price (schema.org billingDuration P1M); the annual-billing price is not in the static page. SCIM DELETE deactivates rather than deletes; group sync works for Jira, Confluence and Trello only, not Bitbucket. Guard Standard allows one identity provider; multiple IdPs need Enterprise. The free Organizations and User management admin APIs are available on all plans. The June row cited /software/access/pricing; the current Guard pricing URL is /software/guard/pricing.

auth.token_expiry: 1 year (auto-set for keys created or regenerated since January 2025)

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivation keeps the account's personal data so it can be reactivated; deleting a user in the IdP, or SCIM DELETE, deactivates the account and unlinks the SCIM record rather than deleting the Atlassian account.

custom.how: No arbitrary custom attributes documented; Atlassian defines its own extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:atlassian:2.0:User (basedIn for location).

roles.how: Group-based: synced groups grant app access (licenses) and admin permissions; no SCIM roles attribute documented.

limitations.text: SCIM DELETE does not delete the account; it deactivates it (same as active=false) and removes the SCIM record.
Group sync is only available for Jira, Confluence and Trello, not Bitbucket.
Group renames are not supported; create a new group, move members, delete the old one.
Developer docs state a 150,000 user limit per directory and 35,000 users per group, while the help centre recommends staying below 1 million users and 290,000 users per group; the two pages disagree.
Guard Standard allows one connected identity provider; multiple IdPs need an Enterprise plan.
Requires a verified domain; updates only apply to users from verified domains.
Filtering supports a single eq match on userName or externalId (users) or displayName (groups); sorting is not supported.

user_api.base_url: https://api.atlassian.com/admin (Organizations API, e.g. /admin/v2/orgs/{orgId}/...); https://api.atlassian.com/users (User management API)

endpoints.purpose: Search for users in an organization
Get details of a user in a directory
Get managed accounts in an organization
Suspend user access in directory (not billed while suspended)
Grant access (app role) to a group
Deactivate a managed account (User management API)

audit_log_api.plan: Atlassian Guard Standard (organization admin activity); user-created activity needs Guard Premium or Enterprise

rate_limits.text: 429 with X-RateLimit headers; last-active-dates 200 req/min per org; events API 10 req/min per user and per path (lowered from 60/50 in May 2025); events-stream 60 req/min per user, 50 per path.

limitations.text: Admin API keys last at most one year.
Audit log webhook integration (push of events) is a Guard Premium feature; no user-lifecycle webhook is documented for the admin APIs.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Workspace directory sync (users and groups) and an Azure AD nested-groups sync option, both from Atlassian Administration

open_questions: Annual-billing price of Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium is not in the static pricing page (only the monthly-billing $4.20/$8.18 is); the June row's $4.20 may be the monthly price.
Whether SCIM deactivation revokes active sessions immediately is not stated explicitly (the deactivate page says access is lost 'immediately' but does not mention sessions).
SCIM rate limits are not documented.
Bulk and /Me SCIM endpoints are not mentioned in the reference; ServiceProviderConfig response body is not shown, so Bulk support is unconfirmed.
OneLogin catalogue page (onelogin.com/connector/...) could not be loaded (bot protection); OneLogin facts come from Atlassian's own docs.
CSV user import for Atlassian Cloud was not researched/verified.
